note: The JavaScript input controls the string value containing a UTF-16 surrogate pair that is converted to the StringPrimitive iterated by Symbol.iterator.
The input-controlled StringPrimitive is stored into a JSStringIterator for later next() calls.
The iterator reads the first UTF-16 code unit from the controlled string at the current position.
Because the first code unit is a high surrogate and another code unit remains, the iterator reads the second controlled code unit.
A two-element stack buffer is used as the backing store for the two-code-unit iterator result, so later string creation must not read more than two char16_t elements from it.
The stack buffer reference is passed to string creation; the target failure is a read past the two-element charArr while copying or classifying the UTF-16 data.
